summary: Iteration 13 — PRODUCTION HARDENING tested end-to-end. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration13.py: 16 PASS / 1 SKIP / 1 FAIL. Frontend Playwright on desktop 1920x1080 verified Customer (no PIN gate, Table 7 lock badge), Kitchen (PIN gate + all 4 testids + wrong/correct PIN flow), and Manager Settings (kitchen-pin-form present, customer-pin-form absent, 'Kitchen Display PIN' label visible, mgr_token persisted in localStorage). One CRITICAL backend bug found: PUT /api/settings is OPEN — it accepts updates WITHOUT an Authorization header (HTTP 200), violating the production-hardening spec which says it must require manager Bearer token. All other gated endpoints (PUT /profile, GET /stats/today, GET /stats/revenue, GET /auth/sessions, PUT /settings/kitchen-pin, POST/PUT/DELETE on /menu and /categories) correctly return 401 without token and succeed with valid token. POST /orders correctly does NOT require manager token (customer-open flow). GET /orders is open (200) — kitchen+customer flow. Kitchen-PIN endpoints work end-to-end: 404 when unset, set via manager-authed PUT, correct PIN -> token, wrong PIN -> 401. GET /api/payments/config returns key_id='', configured=false, fallback_link='' (no hardcoded razorpay.me). GET /api/pricing?tables=20 returns 1888.0. DEMO_MODE=true env confirmed via demo_otp present in /auth/request-otp response.

critical.issue: OPEN endpoint — accepts updates without Authorization header (returns 200). Spec requires manager Bearer token. The route definition at server.py:609 is missing `dependencies=[Depends(_require_manager)]`. Anyone with the public URL can mutate restaurant_name, logo_url, gst_number, phone, address, etc. Verified by sending `PUT /api/settings {restaurant_name:'X'}` with NO auth header — it returned 200 + persisted the change.

action_items: CRITICAL: Add `dependencies=[Depends(_require_manager)]` to @api_router.put('/settings') at server.py line ~609 — currently any unauthenticated caller can update restaurant settings (name, logo, GST, address, phone, printer_type, theme). One-line fix: `@api_router.put('/settings', response_model=RestaurantSettings, dependencies=[Depends(_require_manager)])`. Also update frontend Settings save UX to ensure Bearer is sent (axios interceptor already does this — should be transparent).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py — PUT /api/settings (line 609) MISSING _require_manager guard. This is a production security bug given iteration 13 explicitly hardens manager endpoints. POST/PUT/DELETE for /menu and /categories all use the dependency correctly; /settings was missed.

server.py — PUT /api/orders/{order_id} (line 1010) is gated by _require_subscription but NOT by _require_manager. Per spec this is INTENTIONAL because kitchen status updates go through this endpoint and the kitchen flow has its own PIN, but it means any subscriber's order can be marked done/delivered by anyone who knows the order_id. Document this design choice or add a kitchen-token check.

rca of the issue: RCA — PUT /api/settings OPEN: The route definition `@api_router.put('/settings', response_model=RestaurantSettings)` at server.py:609 was inadvertently NOT updated with `dependencies=[Depends(_require_manager)]` during the iteration 13 hardening pass. All the other manager-only mutations got the guard added (lines 358, 365, 485, 494, 520, 541, 555, 576, 957, 969, 985, 1020, 1123), but /settings PUT was missed. Reproduction: `curl -X PUT https://restaurant-ops-desk.preview.emergentagent.com/api/settings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"restaurant_name":"OWNED"}'` — returns 200 + persists. Mitigation: add `dependencies=[Depends(_require_manager)]` to the @api_router.put('/settings', ...) decorator. The frontend axios interceptor already attaches the Bearer header for SettingsSection saves, so adding the guard is a transparent backend-only change.
